text: Balvinder, can you move the MarkLogic job onto dev-full before Thursday? Rodney asked for the timings, so copy him into the thread when you post them.

Jayendra has checked the reference counts, so Harnadh can start the import this afternoon. Abhishek, if you have a minute before then, could you look at the rollback notes, because I think the retry section is missing a step.

The XQuery module reads the root element first, then sends each record down the new route, so the URIs come out in the same order they went in. Check that the CoRB batch uses the same route before we restart it.

Wrangler is still writing to the staging store, and I think the SPARQL queries we ran this morning were reading from the wrong place. Once the XDBC connection is switched over, the triple counts should line up again.
The staging data is dirty after the failed run, so I want it cleared before the next load. Keep the backup for thirty days, and then we can drop the old exports.

The duplicate contacts have been removed from the feed, and the certificate for the staging host was renewed last night. The second run should go through cleanly, so let me know if the logs look any different.
Abhishek's suggestion for the ingestion step is reasonable. We will batch the incoming files by source, and the content update module stays as it is for now.
Let's merge the two contact lists on the email key rather than the name, because the marketing feed spells half of the names differently. That should stop most of the duplicates.
The leads from the Leeds event are fine to keep, but I would like the duplicates checked against the existing list before anything goes into the pipeline.
The reindex took 2 hours and 10 minutes on dev-full, and the index now holds 1.2 billion triples. We need two more hosts before the 14 November run, so please raise the request this week.

The Frankendoc export is now on v11.2, and the failure rate dropped from 30% to under 2% after the patch. Divya thinks that is the fix, but QA should confirm it on the full dataset before we call it done.
The SAAS dashboard says 14% more documents came in yesterday, which I think is right, because the Datavid connector caught up after the outage.
The CTS query returns documents with a cache, so the first call is slow and the rest are quick. Please do not clear the cache on the production host without asking Balvinder first.
Harnadh has finished the SciFinder mapping, so QA can start the regression pass on the export today. Let me know if the record count does not match the source.

The Posthog events are still not reaching the dashboard, and the Cypher query for the graph export needs a new index before it will run. Can you also check the Schengen data residency rule for the EU client?
Jayendra thinks the reference data is ready, so I will tell Datavid we can start the SPARQL checks on Monday. The triples should match the migration notes, but I would like to see the counts first.

Rodney asked me for a status on the search side, so here it is. The nightly reindex rebuilds the CTS indexes first, then pushes the flattened rows to StarRocks, where the analysts run their queries. Divya ran it on dev-full last night, and it took just under 2 hours, which is fine for now. If the volume doubles, though, I think it becomes a real problem, so we should look at the StarRocks load before the spring. The dashboards read from that table, so any lag shows up there first.

Quick update on the Frankendoc export. The XQuery module that feeds it now sends each batch down the new route, and the URIs come out in order, which fixes the duplicates we saw on Tuesday. Harnadh has cleared the old exports from the staging host, so the ingestion step can run again. Once the second run is clean, Jayendra will check the counts against the source. The leads that came in twice from the marketing feed have been removed, so that should be the end of it, unless QA finds something new.

Abhishek and I went through the SPARQL side this morning. Only Wrangler should write to the store, and the reasoning agent should read from it, so the audit trail stays clean. The XDBC pool needs a short timeout, and, given the larger batch jobs, I would size it for 30% more memory than the laptop test suggested. Balvinder has the ops numbers for the hosts, so I would trust his figures over mine. Please confirm before you change anything in the config.

Notes on the MarkLogic upgrade to v11.2, while they are fresh. Balvinder ran the first rolling restart on dev-full on Tuesday, and it went cleanly, although one host took much longer to come back than the others. The reason was the forest rebalancing, which kicked in as soon as the host rejoined, and it saturated the disk for about 20 minutes. Nothing was lost, and the XDBC clients reconnected on their own, but the retry settings were too short, so a few batch jobs failed and had to be replayed. I would raise the timeout before the production window, and stagger the restarts so that only one host is out at a time. Rodney wants a go or no-go by Friday, so I will write up the numbers tomorrow morning, once the logs are in.

Divya has finished the mapping for the SciFinder export, and I want to get the notes down before I forget the details. The export arrives as nested JSON, not flat rows, so the first version of the mapping dropped every author who was listed under a second affiliation. Divya fixed that by reading the nested records directly, and the record count now matches the source for 98% of the sample. The remaining 2% are mostly records with missing DOIs, and Crossref has no match for them, so we will keep them as they are. QA has the list of mismatches, and Harnadh is going to check the first fifty by hand. Please do not rerun the full load until he has signed them off, because it writes straight into the review collection, and that is awkward to undo.

I have been trying a Claude prompt to turn the raw meeting notes into the weekly status update, and the results are good, but not yet good enough to send unchecked. The model keeps the names right, which is the main thing, but it tends to invent a deadline when the notes do not give one. So I have added an instruction to leave the date blank rather than guess, and that stopped it on the three test notes. It also writes Title Case headings where we use sentence case, which is annoying but easy to fix in the template. Before we roll it out to the team, I would like Rodney to read the output for two weeks, because the failures will be quiet ones.

Here is the plan for the nightly load, and the reason I changed it. The StarRocks load used to run in one long transaction, which meant that a failure at hour two threw away everything before it. We have split it into tables, so each table commits on its own, and the load can resume from the last table that succeeded. Abhishek suggested this after the outage in September, and I think it was the right call, although it means the dashboards can show a partial night for a short while. The Datavid connector still holds one connection open for the whole run, so I have capped it at four, which should stop the other XQuery jobs from being starved. If you see stale totals before 9 in the morning, check the load log first, because that is usually where the answer is.

Notes to self before Monday. The Posthog events for the new search page are still not arriving, and I think the problem is the batch size on our side, because the sender drops anything above two hundred events. Please check that first, before you touch the dashboard. The Cypher export for the graph is a separate piece of work, and we need a new index on the relationship keys before it will finish in a sensible time. The Schengen data residency rule needs checking for the EU client before the export goes live, and the answer is probably in the shared folder, but I have not read it yet. Finally, the QA team wants a sample of twenty records checked by hand, and they would rather get it on Thursday than Friday, so please put that ahead of the Posthog work if you have to choose.

Balvinder asked for a review of the XQuery upgrade branch before the freeze, so here are my comments in the order I found them. The first thing is the retry wrapper, which catches every error and replays it, including the ones that should stop the job. That is the thing I would fix first. Second, the module reads the root element and then the child nodes, but the new schema puts the metadata in a sibling, so the lookup returns the empty sequence on the staging data. Third, the Datavid helper still uses the old route to the REST endpoint, and it should use the new one from the config. Fourth, the duplicate check removes records by URI, not by contact key, which I think is wrong, although I may be missing a reason. Finally, the CoRB property names are mixed case in some places and lower case in others, so please pick one style and apply it across the module.
